hypotheses.construction_plan: Instantiate the single-argument template F(θ) with the two algebraically equivalent inner expressions x*(y+z) and x*y+x*z. This captures the F01 family as two specialization instances of the same undetermined function F.
required_assumptions: F is an undetermined function with one argument
x*(y+z) and x*y+x*z are acceptable inner arguments related by distributivity
hypotheses.rationale: Both F01 members share the same outer undetermined function F and differ only in the algebraic form of the single inner argument. The observed LGG already suggests the template F(θ).

hypotheses.construction_plan: Represent F02 by the linear-in-θ template L(θ)=θ*(y+z). The member x*(y+z) is L(x). The member y+z is generated by differentiating L(θ) with respect to θ, then evaluating at θ=x, since ∂/∂θ[θ*(y+z)] = y+z.
required_assumptions: Differentiation with respect to θ is valid
y and z are treated as independent of θ
hypotheses.rationale: F02 is reported as an exact derivative relation. Representing the two members as a linear monomial in θ and its θ-derivative gives a minimal shared structural template.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Use K(θ)=θ*(y+z) as the shared algebraic kernel. Its identity specialization at θ=x gives x*(y+z); its θ-derivative at θ=x gives y+z; and the same kernel appears inside the undetermined function F, giving F(K(x))=F(x*(y+z)). This connects one member of F01 with the F02 derivative family through the same inner polynomial factor.
required_assumptions: F acts on the same kernel K(θ)
The derivative relation of F02 applies to the kernel K(θ)
hypotheses.rationale: The argument inside F in N0002 is exactly the algebraic object whose derivative relation generates F02. This suggests a shared kernel rather than an accidental overlap.
